reviews.title: Misleading Storage Limits and Hidden Costs with OurFamilyWizard
reviews.text:
Before subscribing, be aware of a major restriction OurFamilyWizard does NOT clearly disclose on its website or pricing page.

The Essentials annual plan advertises **5 GB of secure storage**, but what they don't tell you is that this is a *LIFETIME limit*, NOT an annual allowance!Your storage NEVER renews or resets, even though you pay for a new subscription every year. And 5 GB is NOT enough for years of use.

For a co-parenting app where parents exchange and preserve documents, photos, and important records for years, this is a serious limitation. It is unreasonable and contrary to standard subscription practices to include a feature capped for the lifetime of an account without clearly disclosing it BEFORE purchase.

Once you reach 5 GB, you **HAVE to upgrade** from Essentials ($149.99/year) to Premium ($216/year) to continue uploading files. You're pushed into paying more for something you weren't properly informed about.

I contacted customer service, but they dismissed my concerns without explaining this undisclosed restriction or offering any solution. Completely unhelpful!

There are cheaper alternatives offering similar features:

- **AppClose:** $83.88/year, 44% cheaper than Essentials and 61% cheaper than Premium, with UNLIMITED file storage.
- **TextingParents Premium:** $99/year for both parents, 34% cheaper than Essentials and 54% cheaper than Premium.

The biggest issue is the lack of transparency. Their annual subscription description doesn't clearly explain

reviews.title: I rarely write negative reviews
reviews.text:
If you’re like me, you may be weighing the cost of coparenting counseling against trying this app first. I wish I had understood the pricing more clearly before signing up. Both parents have to pay separately, and the only option is an annual subscription. Together, that came to almost $400 for us, roughly the cost of two coparenting counseling sessions, which have been far more effective.

This was a significant expense during an already difficult financial time. There is a 30-day refund policy, but realistically, while navigating a divorce, I simply didn’t get around to requesting one within that window.

More importantly, the app just wasn’t practical for us. It was too easy to miss important messages that needed attention in real time. In retrospect, I wish we had put that money toward coparenting counseling instead.

reviews.title: Calendar does not give monthly scheduling options
reviews.text:
So the calendar does not let you program in options for a parenting schedule that isn’t weekly. It has no monthly scheduling options at all.

For example, my schedule is to generally have my kids Monday after school until Friday school drop off, with my ex generally having them Friday after school until Monday drop off. That part it could handle.

However, I also get the kids every third weekend of the month, which is impossible to program in, because there are no monthly options for interval.

My ex also gets the kids the first two Mondays of each month, which is also impossible to program in.

As a result, the calendar function is worse than useless.

Please update it so people with monthly intervals can use your app.

reviews.title: Not the app for you if you want equal co parenting
reviews.text: I’ve used this app for a year now, and as a step parent, I continue to be relegated technologically as a second class citizen. When I first got the app, I submitted a request to be able to have notifications. They were pretty straightforward in their response. Though they would consider future requests, their view was that the two biological parents should have complete priority in these features. So if her father requests an item of clothing that might be at my house, I don’t get a badge, a push notification, an email- nothing. The philosophy is flawed and the app is so basic I wouldn’t pay for it otherwise.

reviews.title: Clunky

reviews.title: Buggy- no care for clients
reviews.text:
Ran into several MAJOR issues. My Apple no longer allow me to answer calls… This caused additional stress and issues with my ex, thinking I was trying to avoid calls. I asked to be given minutes to continue to MAKE calls as I was unable to ANSWER any and had used all my minutes. They said they couldn’t do that!!! They took over 2 weeks to reply to my phone calls and messages- with the same “we aren’t sure how to give you minutes at this time”.  It has been over 7 weeks since I have been able to answer a call…. No refund, no extension of service offer—- just SILENCE from a court mandated app designed to keep me safe. Instead causing significant ADDITIONAL conflicts with zero communication, compensation, or humanity.



Update:  got an email from OFW asking me to call in… I have called in MANY times, no help. My request for a manager was answered the next day by email. That manager then stopped communicating and responding. 

I have now FINALLY been given access to MAKE calls, but STILL have no access to ANSWER a call. 

Got an email that an update was made and I should be able to answer calls- nope. It does NOT work. Updated the app, nada. Now I am having major difficulty logging into the app both on my iPhone and my iPad. 

This is causing MAJOR stress in communication and having ripple impacts. NOT ok for a service I am paying A LOT of money for.

reviews.title: No notifications = no point in the app!
reviews.text: Costs over£100 a year & then the app doesn’t bother notifying you of messages & updates, which is the entire point of the app (& yes, all notifications are on, it’s the app that’s not working properly). As such, you miss important updates unless you make a point of checking regularly yourself. Very, very poor service given the cost

reviews.title: Constantly get No Internet Connection popping up
reviews.text: This is despite having strong internet in multiple locations. Tried to refresh app by closing it down and opening it. Running latest version of app on iPhone 18 pro.

reviews.title: Poor message handling
reviews.text:
Every other messaging app gives you notifications and an indicator if there are unread messages. This one just dings once. 
Looking through the conversation thread also requires advanced skills. Took me a while to find out that my messages actually were sent. One has to go to the filter settings each time and bring up all messages. 
Userfriendly is done differently.

reviews.title: Not the best
reviews.text: The app is ok for some things but it feels really outdated. There’s no setup guide so you have to find out and adjust the app as you go along, the apps options are limited, there’s an function to include photos in messages but it never works, emails are not sequential and so appear as a mass of messages. I’m also yet to find how to download records and reports.

reviews.title: overpriced and not user-friendly
reviews.text: For the high price of this app, you would think that they would offer more features and benefits. They’ve chosen not to make it any better at any time because they have a  product which users are forced to use and pay for. There’s no need for them to spend any money on improvement or customer service.  The worst part about it is the text. It is a medium gray color and tiny font which is difficult to see, even though I have excellent vision. There is no way to change the font, color or the size of the text like you can do in every single other messaging app. Due to this there are always mistakes noticed after a message is sent and they’re very difficult to see. A wait time feature would be very nice so that you could edit your message before it is formally sent.  On my caseC my high conflict ex focuses in on my errors and uses them to create a false interpretion of the message or to insult me. Currently, there is no way to edit your messages besides responding to the bad message which then causes the other person to get extra messages that should not have to be sent. And when a high conflict person receives one extra message (no matter that they have sent 20 messages in the past hour) they ignore the original intent and instead start a conversation about harassing with multiple messages. I hate this app.

reviews.title: Creates More Opportunity for Failed Communication
reviews.text: The app will not communicate with more traditional calendar platforms, therefore if you maintain a work calendar or other personal calendar, you have to “export” events- which dont include all of the event details like which children are scheduled or which parents are responsible for drop off or pickup.  You would then have to manually ensure both calendars stay in sync if things change.  As a working professional, I find it extremely cumbersome to have to maintain both.  This “flagship” feature of this app becomes an opportunity for further issues since you have to maintain multiple calendars.    The messaging is fine, but if you need to export a message to a PDF report, you have to login through a browser, that cannot be done through the app which feels like a big miss.  Given the annual price tag for this app, and its seemingly universal mandate by courts, I would have expected a much better and more user friendly set of features.

reviews.title: Another tool of manipulation
reviews.text:
If you’ve been through a rough divorce there’s a good chance you know there’s one person who wants to be left alone, and one that refuses to leave the other alone. Our Family Wizard somehow worked their way into the we of things an ex can obligate you to have and pay for seemingly against your will because you either agree, or keep fighting with a lower to be left alone. 
There is nothing Our Family Wizard offers that couldn’t be handled through text messages, Venmo, and a shared calendar, but instead we have a court order that requires me to pay $150 per year for software I never wanted. I have full parental rights, full custody, and even a protective order against my exs spouse, and I still need to keep this app because they got it into the parenting plan. You’d think with a history like theirs that wouldn’t be necessary, but any inconvenience they are able to force on me they will. That is all Our Family Wizard is to me. An inconvenience, and an additional legal expense.

reviews.title: Poor Quality
reviews.text: I get it while I’m sure a lot of people have to use this, the video quality is very poor, you cannot do a lot on the app, and I have to keep deleting it and re-downloading it because I keep opening it up and it will not open. I keep missing calls from my children and my ex keeps using it against me. This is a court mandated app to use, otherwise I would not use it. I paid for the highest tear of the app & I think it is absolute trash. If I wasn’t forced to use it by the court, I absolutely would not. I don’t recommend it to anybody. While it may have other features such as journaling and splitting costs, all that stuff can be done using other apps that are a lot cheaper, and that don’t fail every time you try to open them. I’ve had to delete, and re-download this app 12 times over the last week. Absolute TRASH! It’s not even like you can get somebody online to help you, because there is no support line listed on the app. It is absolute highway robbery for what I paid for!

reviews.title: Not worth a cent
reviews.text: This app is slow, fails to save login details and worse notifications don’t work so forever having to check which as you can imagine is not conducive to good co parenting. Avoid.

reviews.title: Money for old rope
reviews.text:
An expensive email client you’re forced to use when the other parent doesn’t want to co-parent.
A number of woeful inadequacies for such an expensive service…

1) EMail folders have a 25 character limit, so if you organise messages by events/dates, you’ll soon run out of space…

2) Expenses can be rejected with no space to provide a reason! Considering the legal focus of the app, this is a glaring omission!

3) Useless implementation of “AI” that’s nothing more than a tone/semantic checker. The fact that I send one message and subsequently receive a barrage of messages from the other parent just indicates the gimmick.

4) Calendar doesn’t integrate with device calendar for alarms/notifications.

What’s the point? The other parent can still act in the worst way possible. The content is just as admissible in a court setting!

Concerningly, info online shows the owning company office in London is permanently closed with directors constantly changing on the companies house register. It’s a UK subsidiary that seems to make a loss on its figures. Looks like they are just extracting money from honest people who want to see their kids!

reviews.title: Reliability In Not Optional for a Court-Ordered App
reviews.text:
OurFamilyWizard is a court ordered communication platform, which makes reliability essential. When the app fails, it directly interferes with a parent’s ability to comply with court expectations.

The iOS app has opened to the dashboard but failed to register any user interaction, making it impossible to send or receive messages. I attempted standard troubleshooting steps including restarting the device, force closing the app, and checking for updates, without success. Communication was effectively blocked despite good faith efforts to use the required platform.

If courts expect parents to rely on this app, it must function consistently. When technical failures occur, users need clear guidance and timely resolution. The purpose of OurFamilyWizard is sound, but the mobile app does not currently meet the level of reliability required for a mandated tool.

reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text: In court we pushed for OFW to be required in our situation due to conflict issues in coparenting…the judge agreed and required all communication be through the app. We upgraded our account from the basic account to the level that allows for phone calls to be placed through the app for us to be able to communicate with the children when they weren’t in our care and our coparent never paid for the upgrade therefore we never got to use the upgraded feature once.  We had it for a year and we were never able to use it. We asked OFW if they would credit our account the wasted money on the upgrade to go towards next years fees and they denied our request. Very disappointing to have fought to use this company specifically and then for them to show such a lack of empathy and understanding in this challenging time. We’re no stranger to our coparent breaking custody agreements and not following through…but it’s a shame when we then get punished by having to pay for something that was a total waste for us considering that feature is dependent on both parties paying the upgrade. I’m really hoping they’ll have some compassion and understanding and reconsider.

reviews.title: This app does not comply with UK law. Auto renews without you asking it to & refunds are refused
reviews.text:
This app offers nothing that you can’t do for free with your phone. My ex insisted on it & then stopped using it. I had signed up due to being forced to do so then it auto renewed charging me over £100. I asked for a refund & was told that they do not offer refunds on auto renewals… this is in direct contradiction to UK law & I will be pursuing the matter. 

Do not use this app, it’s a waste of time & a huge waste of money

reviews.title: Court ordered
reviews.text:
Frankly I can’t believe this app is court ordered to use its cost a completely unreasonable amount of money is clunky and out dated and you get charged on both ends for using it this app is just robbing people. Plus top it all off the the doesn’t foster communication but hinders communication with its ridiculous email format text. This app needs to go the way of the dinosaurs and especially when there is better apps out there that don’t cost money!!!

Update: we don’t even use the app any more they send you a email saying there going to charge ya and there is no easy way to end your “subscription “ this app and all the people involved with its court ordered use, are bad people taking advantage of already stressed parents often time this app is the cause for more. Shame on you family gizzard.

reviews.title: Pointless Misery Racket
reviews.text:
This app doesn’t do anything that your phone doesn’t already do, it does exactly what your phone can do, except a million times worse. It’s clunky and doesn’t work/have features that are really beneficial. It’s always a privacy nightmare, being unable to hide logins/message reads, enabled stalking and other abuse. What’s worse, for all of this lovely package, it’s not even free. 

Stop creating a situation to profit from the misery of poor children who have a abhorrent parent who can’t be grown up
